summary: As a WhatsApp automation developer, I acknowledge the pain of building custom retry and queue logic, but the pain isn't severe enough to justify a significant purchase. I would likely continue using my own implementation or a partial competitor like UltraMsg for basic needs. I would only consider buying if the solution is very cheap (under $10/month) and integrates seamlessly with Meta's Cloud API without adding another dependency.
strongest_points: Saves development time: I wouldn't need to build and maintain my own queue and retry system from scratch.
Reduces manual monitoring: Built-in retry and dead-letter queues would cut down on constant checks for failed messages.
Potential reliability improvement: A dedicated solution might handle edge cases better than my ad-hoc implementation.
weaknesses: Low willingness to pay: The economic impact is minimal (score 1/5), so I'm not willing to spend more than a few dollars per month. Most competitors start at $10–$49/month, which feels too high for a niche feature.
Existing workaround is acceptable: I already have a custom queue and retry system that works. Switching would require integration effort and trust in a new provider, which is friction.

Trust and compliance concerns: If the solution uses unofficial WhatsApp gateways (like ChatAPI), I'd worry about account bans or reliability. I'd prefer something built on top of the official Meta Cloud API.
Integration requirements: Must integrate with my existing WhatsApp Business API setup (Meta Cloud API or Twilio). If it's a separate platform, I'd have to manage another vendor.
